A 42-year-old woman presents for follow-up of laboratory results after her initial visit. She reports no
health complaints and has normal vital signs, but mentions a 5-year gap in primary care due to loss of
insurance from unemployment. Her laboratory findings show: - AST: 536 U/L - ALT: 675 U/L - Bilirubin:
1.0 mg/dL - Albumin: 2.3 g/L - HCV Ab: positive Additional test results reveal: - HCV antibody: reactive
- HCV RNA: undetectable - HCV viral load: undetectable - Liver biopsy: mild cirrhosis What is the most
appropriate treatment regimen for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Daclatasvir and sofosbuvir (B)
Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir combination (C) Ribavirin and Peg interferon alfa (D) Elbasvir/grazoprevir
combination (E) Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir combination (F) Peg interferon alfa (G) Simeprevir and
sofosbuvir (H) Sofosbuvir (I) Adefovir and tenofovir (J) Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir combination
 A. Ribavirin and Peg interferon alfa
B. Peg interferon alfa
C. Daclatasvir and sofosbuvir
D. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir combination
E. Sofosbuvir
F. Simeprevir and sofosbuvir
G. Adefovir and tenofovir
H. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir combination

I. Elbasvir/grazoprevir combination
J. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir combination
